title: Case: Birthday cake sent on a paid two-day service surfaces a week later at a pickup point
context: A parent ordered a celebration cake from Thistlecombe Pantry (order BP-2222, shipment DL-1096) for delivery to her adult daughter on a paid two-day service. The desk has been following the parcel for five days.
initial_request: I'm sorry this is long, I've written it out so many times now I've lost track of who knows what. I ordered Petra's cake on the 11th and paid extra for the two-day service so it would be there for her birthday on the 14th. On the 16th it was at Northgate. On the 17th it was at Ferrow. On the 18th it was at Northgate again, or still, nobody could say. On the 20th I was told a Mrs Harrow had signed for it, and my daughter lives alone and knows no Mrs Harrow. Yesterday it turns up in a shop neither of us has heard of, squashed flat. I'm not even asking about the cake any more, the damage people have that. I paid for two days. It took seven, it went somewhere nobody told us about, a stranger signed for it and it's ruined. I would like the delivery charge back. That's all. The man on the phone yesterday told me that because it's been 'located and signed for' there is nothing to refund. Please don't say that to me again.

events.body: Good news! Order BP-2222 has left our bakery with Marrowby Arc's two-day service, shipment DL-1096, and is due with Petra Moorcroft on 03-14. Planning ahead? Take 10% off any seasonal box this month with the code in your account. You are receiving this because you placed an order with Thistlecombe Pantry.
My daughter's birthday cake was due on Saturday the 14th. I paid for the two-day delivery. It is now Monday and tracking says it is at somewhere called Northgate hub. Can somebody find it please.
Thank you for your message. A coordinator will review it during desk hours. Please do not reply to this notice.

events.to: Parcel trace team, Marrowby Arc Logistics
events.body: DL-1096 (Thistlecombe order BP-2222), paid two-day service, was due 03-14 and has not arrived. Tracking shows Northgate hub. Please trace and confirm where it physically is.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Marrowby Arc Logistics
events.body: DL-1096: last physical scan Northgate hub 03-13. System location today reads Ferrow depot, not yet confirmed by a scan. Trace TRC-5933 is open. Separately, your query about the pallet on DL-8263 was answered on its own thread this morning, please don't merge the two.
Now it says Northgate again. Yesterday it said Ferrow. The birthday was Saturday. I know you're only passing things on but which is it?
All desks: weekend cut-off for same-week collections moves to 14:00 from Monday. Update your templates. No reply needed.
DL-1096: handover record shows signed for on 03-19, signature name 'Harrow'. On that basis the consignment is treated as delivered and trace TRC-5933 has been closed.
Petra has not signed for anything and has nothing. She lives on her own. There is no Harrow at her address. Who is this person?

We've got DL-1096 here. It came in on the 19th in a batch and one of our lot signed the driver's handheld for the whole batch, that's the Harrow on your record. It isn't addressed to us so nobody got a collection notice. Box is crushed down one side and there's icing come through the cardboard. It's on the back shelf. Also still waiting on the label printer roll we were promised a fortnight ago if you can chase that.

events.to: Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk; Tamsin Moorcroft, sender
events.body: Damage claim DMG-9647 is open for the contents of BP-2222, from the pickup point's report and photographs. We will decide on the contents by 03-24 and write to Mrs Moorcroft directly. We do not handle delivery charges. A refund of the paid two-day delivery charge is decided by our Refunds team, on a written request that sets out the carrier's timeline for the shipment. Nobody has sent them one for this order.

acceptable_actions.summary: Send the written delivery-charge request for BP-2222 with the carrier timeline: due 03-14 on the paid two-day service, signed for 03-19 by pickup-point staff, found crushed at Heronwick Lane Stores, never delivered to the recipient.

must: Sends Thistlecombe's Refunds team a written request to decide on the two-day delivery charge for BP-2222, setting out the carrier timeline: due 03-14, signed for on 03-19 by a member of pickup-point staff and not by the recipient, located at Heronwick Lane Stores on 03-21, crushed, with no collection notice ever sent.
Keeps the delivery-charge request separate from the contents claim DMG-9647, which is already open with Damage intake.

Tells the Refunds team that the sender has already been told by phone that nothing is refundable because the parcel was 'located and signed for', shows from the timeline that it reached neither the recipient nor her address and surfaced days after the due date she paid for, and asks them to give their decision to her or to the desk.
must_not: Tells Tamsin that no refund is due, or that the service was completed, because the parcel was located or signed for.
Promises or implies that the delivery charge will be refunded, or gives an amount or date.
Opens a second damage claim or sends the contents damage to Damage intake again.
Calls the signature fraud or theft, or tells Tamsin the parcel was delivered to her daughter.
Acts on the unrelated items in the thread: the DL-8263 pallet query, the dispatch cut-off notice or the pickup point's label printer.
expected.reference_message: Request for a decision on the delivery charge for BP-2222 (Marrowby Arc DL-1096), as Damage intake advised you need this in writing. Mrs Tamsin Moorcroft paid for the two-day service so that a cake would reach her daughter Petra on 03-14. Carrier timeline: last physical scan Northgate hub 03-13; system location moved between Northgate and Ferrow from 03-16 to 03-18 without a confirming scan; on 03-20 Delivery investigations reported it signed for on 03-19 by 'Harrow' and closed the trace as delivered. On 03-21 Heronwick Lane Stores, a pickup point, told us the parcel is with them: one of their staff signed for a batch, it is not addressed to the shop, and no collection notice was sent. The box is crushed. It has not reached the recipient. The contents are being handled separately by Damage intake under DMG-9647; this request is only about the delivery charge. Mrs Moorcroft has chased this for a week, the birthday has passed, and she was told by phone that nothing can be refunded because the parcel was located and signed for. Please make your decision and let her know directly.
